title: Thunder and Anansi: The Gifted Stick
subtitle: Repeated trouble follows repeated choices

stick.author: W. H. Barker and Cecilia Sinclair
stick.translator: not applicable; collected, arranged, and retold in English
stick.locator: Story IV · THUNDER AND ANANSI; Story IV · THUNDER AND ANANSI, normalized characters 5276-5850
stick.excerpt: This time, however, he presented Anansi with a fine stick and bade him good-bye. Anansi could scarcely wait till he got into the boat—so anxious was he to try the magic properties of his new gift. “Stick, stick,” he said, “what you used to do for your master do for me also.” The stick began to beat him so severely that, in a few minutes, he was obliged to jump into the water and swim ashore, leaving boat and stick to drift away where they pleased. Then he returned sorrowfully homeward, bemoaning his many bruises and wishing he had acted more wisely from the beginning.
stick.note: Verbatim text from Barker and Sinclair's 1917 English collection of Gold Coast stories. Attribute any specific community only where the collection does so.

narrativeBlocks.title: A gift from Thunder
narrativeBlocks.body: Thunder — the storm-power personified — gives Anansi a stick: a gift with power in it, the kind of present that changes a trickster's fortunes.

narrativeBlocks.title: The power in the stick
narrativeBlocks.body: The stick is no ordinary gift: it carries Thunder's own might — and Anansi, being Anansi, immediately begins to think what such a tool can win for him.

narrativeBlocks.title: The catch in every gift
narrativeBlocks.body: But a power's gift always has its condition or its price — and in the Gold Coast tales, what Thunder gives, Thunder's own logic governs: the stick is dangerous to wield carelessly.

narrativeBlocks.title: The trickster overreaches
narrativeBlocks.body: As always in the cycle, Anansi's ambition with the gift outruns his caution — and the story follows the consequences of a spider playing at storm-power.

narrativeBlocks.title: The gods' gifts are tests
narrativeBlocks.body: Thunder's stick is a fairy-tale pattern in West African dress: the powerful give gifts that test the receiver — and the trickster is always the most interesting test-subject.
